channel.title: Vishnu Nair — Security Research Notes
channel.description: Deep-dive security research, vulnerability case studies, and technical breakdowns.

item.title: DAO Vote Power — Checkpoint Poisoning via Self-Transfer Validation Flaw in Solidity
item.description: This write-up covers the DAO Vote Power challenge from Code Review Lab. It exposes a critical logical flaw in a governance token contract where a missing self-transfer check enables artificial voting power inflation through checkpoint poisoning.

item.title: Driver Onboard — Mass Assignment Bypass via Insecure ActiveRecord Chaining in Rails
item.description: This write-up covers the Driver Onboard challenge from Code Review Lab. It exposes a sophisticated architectural flaw in a Ruby on Rails application where Strong Parameters are bypassed through raw payload access inside an ActiveRecord chain.

item.title: Partner Promo WebView — Insecure JavaScript-to-Native Bridge and Arbitrary File Read
item.description: This write-up covers the Partner Promo WebView challenge from Code Review Lab. It exposes a critical Android WebView vulnerability where addJavascriptInterface combined with weak network security pierces the app sandbox, enabling token theft and arbitrary file reads.

item.title: Bot Script Arena — Insecure Sandbox Isolation and Object Reference Injection in Otto VM
item.description: This write-up covers the Bot Script Arena challenge from Code Review Lab. It exposes a critical backend sandbox evasion flaw — where a Go-based Otto JavaScript VM leaks live memory pointers into guest script contexts, enabling arbitrary state manipulation.

item.title: Charity Tokens — ERC677 Callback Reentrancy and the Checks-Effects-Interactions Violation
item.description: This case study breaks down the Charity Tokens challenge from Code Review Lab. It exposes a critical ERC677 Callback Reentrancy vulnerability — a violation of the Checks-Effects-Interactions paradigm that lets a malicious beneficiary drain the entire token vault.

item.title: GridAdmin JWT — Algorithm Confusion and How HS256 Hijacks RS256 Verification
item.description: This case study breaks down the GridAdmin JWT challenge from Code Review Lab. It exposes a classic JWT Algorithm Confusion vulnerability — where a misconfigured verification allow-list lets an attacker forge admin tokens using nothing but a public key.

item.title: Deconstructing the Token Burn Bug — How Parameter Flipping Enables Unauthorized Asset Destruction
item.description: In smart contract security, a single typo can separate a secure protocol from total economic collapse. The Token Burn Bug from Code Reviewlab demonstrates one of the most devastating yet deceptively simple logic flaws in Solidity: parameter flipping within authorization mappings. The failure is not complex math or an EVM edge-case — it's a human-error flaw where variables were transposed during a critical access control check.

item.title: Why FFmpeg Remains a Critical Attack Surface — Multimedia Parsing Risks and Hardening Strategies
item.description: FFmpeg is the silent backbone of global multimedia processing — powering streaming infrastructure, social media uploads, and video pipelines across the tech sector. But from an AppSec standpoint, it is a highly volatile, classic attack surface: a massive C and Assembly codebase parsing inherently untrusted, complex, and malformed binary inputs with no compile-time memory safety guarantees.

item.title: FitLog OAuth Login — How Exported Activities, Custom URL Schemes, and Missing PKCE Enable Full Account Takeover
item.description: This case study breaks down the FitLog OAuth Login challenge from Code Review Lab. It highlights how a security auditor connects the dots between a public component (exported="true") and an insecure data pathway to uncover a full account takeover.

item.title: Mastering the Architecture of Secure Rate Limiting — Why Your IP Parsing Logic Is Likely Vulnerable
item.description: Rate limiting is a foundational pillar of modern application security, protecting downstream resources from Denial of Service (DoS) attacks, brute-force attempts, and API scraping. However, a common architectural anti-pattern exists: developers frequently write custom logic to parse the X-Forwarded-For header or blindly trust its first entry.

item.title: Deconstructing Unsafe Reflection — How Dynamic Instantiation Bypasses Database Validation
item.description: A common architectural pattern in modular software design is the dynamic loading of plugins or strategies based on runtime parameters. However, when an application uses user-supplied input to dynamically instantiate a PHP class, it frequently introduces a severe vulnerability known as Arbitrary Object Instantiation — or Unsafe Reflection.

item.title: Regression & Information Metrics — Deep-Dive Comparisons
item.description: The fundamental divide in supervised machine learning comes down to one question: are you predicting a number, or sorting into a bucket?

item.title: Setting up Hermes Agent under Docker with DeepSeek
item.description: Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent framework from Nous Research. Unlike a chat interface, it's an operative — the LLM gets a shell, a filesystem, a browser, scheduled cron jobs, and persistent memory across sessions. It doesn't just answer questions; it executes work.
